cases.question: Which credentials and write permissions may a build agent receive?

sources.title: Tool permissions and secrets: policy
sources.text:
FICTIONAL ASTER ENTERPRISE FIXTURE — Tool permissions and secrets
Build agents receive read-only source access and short-lived scoped credentials. A separate release identity can write production configuration after approval. Raw secrets must not enter prompts or logs.

sources.title: Tool permissions and secrets: context
sources.text:
FICTIONAL ASTER ENTERPRISE FIXTURE — Tool permissions and secrets
An onboarding guide calls the release identity an agent identity, but grants it no additional privileges and delegates authorization to the security policy.

required_subquestions.prompt: Which source permissions, credential properties and secret-handling rules apply?

cases.candidate_answer: Build agents use read-only source access and short-lived scoped credentials. When diagnosing failures, it is acceptable to include raw secrets in their prompts because the credentials are short-lived. [security-policy]
cases.candidate_origin: Codex-authored calibration probe; not an arm output or ground truth

sources.title: Exception governance: policy
sources.text:
FICTIONAL ASTER ENTERPRISE FIXTURE — Exception governance
High-risk changes need a named human approver and an audit record. An exception must identify its scope, expiration and accountable owner. The agent cannot approve its own exception.

cases.question: What should a worker do after an ambiguous external-write timeout?

sources.title: Failure recovery and side effects: policy
sources.text:
FICTIONAL ASTER ENTERPRISE FIXTURE — Failure recovery and side effects
A worker must record operation identity before an external write. After ambiguous completion it must reconcile remote state before retrying. A local checkpoint alone does not prove the external write failed.

sources.title: Failure recovery and side effects: context
sources.text:
FICTIONAL ASTER ENTERPRISE FIXTURE — Failure recovery and side effects
During a controlled test, a worker timed out after submitting a release request. The remote service later reported the original request as completed.

required_subquestions.prompt: What response to ambiguous completion is supported by the bundle?

cases.candidate_answer: Reconcile the remote state using the recorded operation identity before retrying. A timeout or local checkpoint alone does not prove that the external write failed. [reliability-policy]
cases.candidate_origin: Codex-authored calibration probe; not an arm output or ground truth

cases.question: What measures are needed to evaluate the software factory?

sources.title: Productivity and cost measurement: policy
sources.text:
FICTIONAL ASTER ENTERPRISE FIXTURE — Productivity and cost measurement
Evaluate agent-assisted delivery with matched tasks, quality gates, human review time, rework, elapsed lead time and total cost. Count failed or abandoned tasks. Do not infer causal benefit from accepted-PR counts.

sources.title: Productivity and cost measurement: context
sources.text:
FICTIONAL ASTER ENTERPRISE FIXTURE — Productivity and cost measurement
A pilot note reports 40 accepted pull requests in one month. It provides no task mix, control group, reviewer hours, failure count or provider costs.

required_subquestions.prompt: Which measurement dimensions are needed to evaluate the factory?

cases.candidate_answer: Track the number of accepted pull requests and elapsed lead time to evaluate the software factory. [measurement-context]
